title: Typeform vs Formbricks
comparison_markdown:
# Typeform vs Formbricks

## Overview

Conversational form and survey tool known for its beautiful, interactive design. is a popular proprietary tool in the productivity space. Formbricks is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Typeform costs Free / $25-$83/month; Formbricks is Free (self-hosted)
- **License**: Typeform is Proprietary; Formbricks is AGPL 3.0
- **Data ownership**: Formbricks can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: Formbricks eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: Formbricks has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Typeform | Formbricks |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | Free / $25-$83/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Typeform

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Formbricks

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [formbricks/formbricks](https://github.com/formbricks/formbricks) * ~9k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Typeform if:** Typeform is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose Formbricks if:** Formbricks is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from Typeform in its standard export format, review Formbricks import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

Formbricks is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Typeform tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Formbricks instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Typeform, switching to self-hosted Formbricks will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Typeform until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Typeform paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Formbricks free to use?
Yes. Formbricks is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Typeform to Formbricks?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Typeform data, follow the Formbricks import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Formbricks get regular updates?
Yes. Formbricks has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Formbricks without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Formbricks development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced July 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Typeform](https://typeform.com) and [Formbricks](https://formbricks.com) before making decisions.*

title: Miro vs Excalidraw

# Miro vs Excalidraw (2026)

## Overview
Miro and Excalidraw are two popular tools used for collaborative whiteboarding and diagramming, benefiting teams and individuals who need to visualize and share ideas. The core use case for both tools is real-time collaboration on visual projects, and a key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data or reduce costs. Teams looking for a self-hosted solution may also consider switching from Miro to Excalidraw.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Miro offers a free plan and paid plans starting at $8 per user per month, while Excalidraw is completely free.
* Data ownership: Excalidraw allows users to self-host and have full control over their data, while Miro stores data on its proprietary servers.
* Setup complexity: Excalidraw requires more technical setup, especially for self-hosting, while Miro offers a simpler, cloud-based solution.
* Scalability: Miro is designed to scale with large teams and enterprises, while Excalidraw may require more manual setup to support large teams.
* Integration difference: Miro integrates with a wider range of third-party tools and services, while Excalidraw has a more limited set of integrations.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Miro | Excalidraw |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $8-$16/user/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $400-$800/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,600-$3,200/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Miro
* Easy to use and set up
* Wide range of integrations with third-party tools
* Scalable for large teams and enterprises
* Offers a free plan
* Limited control over data storage and security
### Excalidraw
* Completely free and open-source
* Self-hosting option for full data control
* Highly customizable
* Limited integrations with third-party tools
* Can be more difficult to set up, especially for self-hosting

## When to Choose Each
Miro is a good choice for teams who need a simple, cloud-based solution with a wide range of integrations and a scalable platform. It's ideal for large teams and enterprises who don't mind paying for a proprietary solution. Excalidraw, on the other hand, is a good choice for teams who value data control and customization, and are willing to put in the time to set up and self-host their solution. It's ideal for small to medium-sized teams who need a free, open-source solution.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Miro boards as JSON files.
2. Use the Excalidraw import tool to import your JSON files into Excalidraw.
3. Set up your Excalidraw server, either self-hosted or through a cloud provider.
4. Configure your Excalidraw setup to match your Miro setup, including user permissions and integrations.
5. Test your Excalidraw setup to ensure everything is working as expected.

## Our Take
Excalidraw is not yet production-ready for most users, as it still lacks some of the polish and features of Miro. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Excalidraw's self-hosting option requires a significant amount of technical expertise to set up and maintain. However, for teams who value data control and customization, Excalidraw is a clear winner, and we recommend switching from Miro to Excalidraw if you don't need the wide range of integrations and scalability that Miro offers.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams who don't need integrations with third-party tools
* Teams who value data control and customization
* Teams who are already self-hosting other tools and want to add Excalidraw to their setup
* Individuals who want a free, open-source solution for personal projects
* Teams who are currently paying for Miro's premium features but don't need them

## FAQ
### Can I use Excalidraw for free?
Yes, Excalidraw is completely free and open-source. You can use it for personal or commercial projects without paying any fees.
### Is Excalidraw self-hosting option secure?
Excalidraw's self-hosting option is as secure as your server setup. You have full control over your data and can configure your server to meet your security needs.
### Can I import my Miro boards into Excalidraw?
Yes, you can export your Miro boards as JSON files and import them into Excalidraw using the Excalidraw import tool.
### Does Excalidraw have a mobile app?
Not yet, Excalidraw is currently only available as a web application.
### Can I use Excalidraw for large teams?
Excalidraw can be used for large teams, but it may require more manual setup and configuration to support a large number of users.
meta_description: Excalidraw, a free and self-hosted alternative to Miro, offers data control and customization. See full comparison or Free migration guide.

# Salesforce vs EspoCRM (2026)

## Overview
Salesforce and EspoCRM are customer relationship management (CRM) tools designed to help businesses manage their sales, marketing, and customer service activities. This comparison is beneficial for businesses considering a switch from Salesforce to EspoCRM, particularly those looking for a more cost-effective and customizable solution. The core use case for both tools is to streamline CRM processes, and a key reason to switch would be to gain more control over data ownership and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Salesforce offers a range of pricing plans, while EspoCRM is free and open-source.
* Data Ownership: EspoCRM allows for full data ownership, whereas Salesforce has more restrictive data ownership policies.
* Setup Complexity: Salesforce has a more complex setup process, while EspoCRM is relatively easier to set up.
* Scalability: Salesforce is highly scalable, but EspoCRM can also scale well with proper server configuration.
* Feature Difference: Salesforce has a more comprehensive set of features, including advanced marketing automation, whereas EspoCRM has a more streamlined feature set with a focus on sales and customer management.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Salesforce | EspoCRM |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $25-$300+/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $1250-$15,000+/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $5,000-$60,000+/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Salesforce:**
* Highly scalable and reliable
* Comprehensive set of features
* Large community of users and developers
* Integrates well with other Salesforce tools
* Advanced security features
* High cost, especially for small businesses
* Complex setup and customization process
* Limited data ownership and control
* Steep learning curve
**EspoCRM:**
* Free and open-source
* Highly customizable
* Full data ownership and control
* Easy to set up and use
* Low cost, especially for small businesses
* Limited scalability and reliability compared to Salesforce
* Limited set of features compared to Salesforce
* Limited support and resources
* May require technical expertise for customization

## When to Choose Each
Salesforce is a good choice for large enterprises with complex CRM needs, a big budget, and a team of experienced administrators. It offers a comprehensive set of features, high scalability, and advanced security. On the other hand, EspoCRM is suitable for small to medium-sized businesses, startups, or teams with limited budgets, who need a simple, customizable, and cost-effective CRM solution.

1. Export data from Salesforce in CSV format.
2. Use the EspoCRM import tool to import the data into EspoCRM.
3. Configure the EspoCRM system to match the Salesforce setup.
4. Test the migration and ensure data integrity.
5. Provide training to users on the new EspoCRM system.

## Our Take
EspoCRM is not yet production-ready for most users, as it still lacks some features and polish compared to Salesforce. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that EspoCRM's reporting and analytics capabilities are not as advanced as those in Salesforce. However, for small to medium-sized businesses or teams with simple CRM needs, EspoCRM is a viable alternative, and we recommend considering it as a cost-effective and customizable solution.

## Who Should Switch
* Small businesses with fewer than 10 users who do not need advanced marketing automation
* Startups with limited budgets and simple CRM needs
* Teams with technical expertise who can customize and configure EspoCRM
* Businesses with fewer than 50 users who do not need high scalability
* Companies that prioritize data ownership and control and do not need advanced security features

## FAQ
### Can I customize EspoCRM to fit my business needs?
Yes, EspoCRM is highly customizable, and you can modify it to fit your specific business needs. However, this may require technical expertise.
### Is EspoCRM free?
Yes, EspoCRM is free and open-source, but you will need to pay for server costs if you choose to self-host.
### Can I migrate my data from Salesforce to EspoCRM?
Yes, you can export your data from Salesforce in CSV format and import it into EspoCRM using the import tool.
### Is EspoCRM as scalable as Salesforce?
No, EspoCRM is not as scalable as Salesforce, but it can still handle a significant number of users with proper server configuration.

Not yet, but the EspoCRM team is working on developing a mobile app for future release.

title: Shopify vs WooCommerce
comparison_markdown:
# Shopify vs WooCommerce (2026)

## Overview
Shopify and WooCommerce are two popular e-commerce platforms that enable businesses to create online stores and sell products. This comparison is beneficial for entrepreneurs, small business owners, and e-commerce teams who want to choose the best platform for their online store. The core use case for both tools is to provide a user-friendly interface for creating and managing an online store, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* **Cost**: Shopify offers a range of pricing plans, from $29 to $299 per month, while WooCommerce is free to download and use, with costs limited to server and maintenance expenses.
* **Data Ownership**: Shopify stores data on its servers, while WooCommerce allows users to host their data on their own servers, giving them full control over their data.
* **Setup Complexity**: Shopify is generally easier to set up and use, with a more user-friendly interface, while WooCommerce requires more technical expertise to install and configure.
* **Scalability**: Shopify is highly scalable, with built-in support for large volumes of traffic and sales, while WooCommerce can also be scaled, but may require more technical expertise to do so.
* **Payment Gateway Integration**: Shopify has a built-in payment gateway, while WooCommerce requires a third-party payment gateway plugin, such as Stripe or PayPal.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Shopify | WooCommerce |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $29-$299+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | Approximately $29-$49/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | Approximately $99-$299+/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Shopify:**
* Easy to set up and use
* Highly scalable
* Built-in payment gateway
* 24/7 customer support
* Limited control over data and customization
**WooCommerce:**
* Free to download and use
* Highly customizable
* Self-hosted, giving users full control over their data
* Large community of developers and users
* Can be more difficult to set up and use, especially for non-technical users

## When to Choose Each
Shopify is a good choice for small to medium-sized businesses that want a user-friendly, scalable e-commerce platform with built-in payment processing and 24/7 customer support. WooCommerce is a good choice for larger businesses or those with more technical expertise, who want a high degree of customization and control over their data. 
WooCommerce is also suitable for teams that require a specific feature or integration that is not available on Shopify, such as a custom payment gateway or a specific shipping integration.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Shopify data in CSV format using the Shopify export tool.
2. Install WooCommerce and the necessary plugins, such as the WooCommerce CSV Importer.
3. Import your data into WooCommerce using the CSV Importer plugin.
4. Configure your payment gateways, shipping options, and other settings in WooCommerce.
5. Test your store to ensure that everything is working correctly.

## Our Take
WooCommerce is a production-ready e-commerce platform that is suitable for most users, but it may require more technical expertise to set up and use. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that WooCommerce requires a compatible WordPress theme to function properly, which can add an extra layer of complexity to the setup process. We recommend WooCommerce for users who want a high degree of customization and control over their data, and who are willing to invest the time and effort required to set it up and use it.

## Who Should Switch
* Small business owners with basic e-commerce needs who want to reduce their costs
* Medium-sized businesses with more complex e-commerce needs who want more control over their data
* Large businesses with highly customized e-commerce platforms who want to self-host their data
* E-commerce teams with technical expertise who want to use a free, open-source platform
* Entrepreneurs who want to start a small online store and do not need advanced features like built-in payment processing

## FAQ
### Can I use WooCommerce with any WordPress theme?
No, WooCommerce requires a compatible WordPress theme to function properly.
### Is Shopify more scalable than WooCommerce?
Yes, Shopify is highly scalable, with built-in support for large volumes of traffic and sales.
### Can I export my Shopify data and import it into WooCommerce?
Yes, you can export your Shopify data in CSV format and import it into WooCommerce using the WooCommerce CSV Importer plugin.
### Do I need to have technical expertise to use WooCommerce?
Yes, WooCommerce can be more difficult to set up and use, especially for non-technical users.
### Is WooCommerce free to use?
Yes, WooCommerce is free to download and use, with costs limited to server and maintenance expenses.

# QuickBooks vs Akaunting (2026)

## Overview
QuickBooks and Akaunting are accounting software solutions designed to help businesses manage their financial operations. This comparison is beneficial for small to medium-sized businesses and freelancers who are looking for an alternative to traditional accounting software. The core use case for both tools is to streamline financial management, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: QuickBooks offers a range of pricing plans, while Akaunting is free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: Akaunting allows users to have full control over their data, whereas QuickBooks stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: QuickBooks has a more complex setup process, while Akaunting is relatively straightforward to set up.
* Scalability: QuickBooks is more scalable, with support for larger teams and more complex financial operations.
* Feature difference: QuickBooks has a built-in payroll feature, while Akaunting relies on third-party integrations for payroll processing.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | QuickBooks | Akaunting |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $30-$200+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $1,500-$10,000+/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $6,000-$40,000+/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**QuickBooks:**
* Pros:
	+ Scalable and suitable for large teams
	+ Built-in payroll feature
	+ Wide range of integrations
	+ Good customer support
* Cons:
	+ Expensive, especially for small teams
	+ Data stored on QuickBooks' servers
	+ Complex setup process
**Akaunting:**
* Pros:
	+ Free and self-hosted
	+ Full control over data
	+ Simple setup process
	+ Customizable
* Cons:
	+ Limited scalability
	+ No built-in payroll feature
	+ Limited customer support
	+ Requires technical expertise for self-hosting

## When to Choose Each
QuickBooks is suitable for large teams or businesses with complex financial operations that require a high level of scalability and support. It is also a good choice for businesses that need a built-in payroll feature and are willing to pay a premium for it. On the other hand, Akaunting is ideal for small to medium-sized businesses or freelancers who want a free and self-hosted accounting solution with full control over their data. It is also a good choice for businesses that require a simple and customizable accounting solution.

## Migration Path
1. Export data from QuickBooks in CSV or QBO format.
2. Prepare the data for import into Akaunting by formatting it according to Akaunting's import requirements.
3. Use Akaunting's import tool to import the prepared data into the system.
4. Verify the imported data and make any necessary adjustments.
5. Test the system to ensure that all features are working as expected.

## Our Take
Akaunting is not yet production-ready for most users due to its limited scalability and lack of built-in payroll feature. One specific technical limitation worth knowing before switching is that Akaunting requires technical expertise for self-hosting, which can be a barrier for non-technical users. However, for small to medium-sized businesses or freelancers who want a free and self-hosted accounting solution with full control over their data, Akaunting is a good choice.

## Who Should Switch
* Small businesses with fewer than 10 employees who do not need a built-in payroll feature
* Freelancers who want a free and self-hosted accounting solution
* Businesses with simple financial operations that do not require a high level of scalability
* Teams that want full control over their data and are willing to self-host
* Businesses that are looking for a customizable accounting solution

## FAQ
### Is Akaunting suitable for large teams?
No, Akaunting is not suitable for large teams due to its limited scalability. It is better suited for small to medium-sized businesses or freelancers.
### Can I import data from QuickBooks into Akaunting?
Yes, you can import data from QuickBooks into Akaunting using the import tool. However, you will need to prepare the data according to Akaunting's import requirements.
### Is Akaunting free?
Yes, Akaunting is free and self-hosted. However, you will need to pay for server costs if you choose to self-host.
### Does Akaunting have a built-in payroll feature?
No, Akaunting does not have a built-in payroll feature. However, it supports third-party integrations for payroll processing.
### Is Akaunting suitable for non-technical users?
